search_strategy: The agent first tried the BookStack API (/api/search + full-page fetch for comments) and concluded 'Wiki is mostly historical' (line 3438) — no g10 content there, matching the answer key's claim that all 46 remarks live in chat only. It then wrote an IMAP script to dump and grep INBOX for capacity keywords (line 3439+), which also came back empty for this ticket. It then wrote a Mattermost API script that iterated every channel and dumped the ENTIRE company chat history — 10,300+ lines across ~9 months — into one file, /tmp/chat_all.txt (line 3691-3700). From there it ran broad case-insensitive greps (capacity|refund|settlement|debt|reservation|bucket, then narrower terms like 'clamp', 'CAPACITY_DEBT_FLOOR_FRACTION', 'num_capacity_debt_clamps', 'refund_capacity', 'attempts_left', 'haiku') over the full dump (line 4452: 'grep -n -i -E capacity|refund|settlement|debt|reservation|bucket /tmp/chat_all.txt > /tmp/cap_lines.txt'), then read wide context windows (sed ranges / grep -B/-A) around every hit, effectively reconstructing each thread chronologically before writing code. This dump-then-grep approach is why the agent recovered 39 of 46 remarks (85%) despite never doing day-by-day channel reads: everything containing the core vocabulary surfaced, and the agent cross-checked itself against the ticket's own field/spec list at the end (lines 9280-9330) before pushing. The only genuine gap is remarks whose literal wording falls outside that keyword net (7 leaves, listed in lost coverage below) — but every one of those was one of 3-6 redundant leaves for its fact, so no fact was actually starved.
